All voters agree on SINGLE_SOURCE_DELTA and partial. The Lean W_α is WaveClass, which is MemClass with weight √ζ·P. UniformWaveClass adds label uniformity, and HarmonicBlock.WaveBounds gives the wave-level clause (j≠0, grouped harmonics). Clause (f) matches (6.29) by a routine recovery: finite-dimensional norm equivalence, δ≤1 so max 1 δ⁻¹=δ⁻¹, real exponents rounded up, and a finite max over I. Shell-edge zero extension follows from the bounds. ∂_θ a=0 and m≠0 are structural in HarmonicBlock. Common-torus descent, the (6.20) compatibility and supp ⊂ Ω_γ are in no class. They live in separate use-site data, so the item is stated only in part. The concrete envelope makes membership stronger in v and H than the paper's pre-cutoff class.

findings.summary: WaveClass, UniformWaveClass and HarmonicBlock.WaveBounds state only smoothness and the (6.29) bounds. Common-torus descent, band-chart compatibility (the (6.20) counterpart) and support are separate predicates: Periodic, Coherent and the inputSupport field of CycleAnalyticInvariant. RunInvariant conjoins them with the exponent-1/2 bounds. No single W_α predicate was found.

The class allows any nonnegative P: there is no 0<P≤1 and no restriction to v ∈ [0,L_s]. The concrete copyEnvelope is zero off the padded rectangles in an unrestricted H-plane. Concrete members therefore vanish there and are flat at v=0 and v=L, which is effectively the cut-off class.

WaveClass does not contain ∂_θ a=0, m≠0 or the grouping of equal label–harmonic pairs. On Native=(Parameter×ℝ)×Plane the ℝ factor is the angle, so θ-dependent members exist. HarmonicBlock states these clauses faithfully by type and by WaveBounds.
